value: hourly mean detections peaked during crepuscular periods
method: passive acoustic telemetry: external coded acoustic transmitters (Innovasea V8-4H) on wild-caught palenose parrotfish, positions from a receiver array; hourly mean detections
conditions: Wild palenose parrotfish at Puako, leeward coast of the Island of Hawai'i (South Kohala). Eight palenose parrotfish tagged (of 16 parrotfish captured at night with mesh nets, the other eight being ember parrotfish) on 13 June (four fish) and 17 June 2012 (four fish) and tracked from 12 June to 15 July 2012 (printed '6/12/2012 to 7/15/2012'; positioning system in place for 35 days). The same abstract sentence says the peak held 'to a lesser extent' for ember parrotfish (Scarus rubroviolaceus), which is not filed here. Preceding abstract sentence: home ranges and core use of both species were significantly larger during the day than at night. Abstract also says both species were mostly detected on the fore reef during the day with no reef-flat use at night, and that night data were too sparse to estimate activity spaces; the peak is read by the authors as movement between shallower daytime (foraging) and nighttime (resting) areas. The abstract opens with the background remark that parrotfishes are known to be strictly diurnal. Methods: each fish was brought back to shore and placed in holding tanks, measured and tagged, and released the following morning in the general location of the capture site (one night in holding tanks, then free-ranging). Table 1 tagging dates: SP1 to SP4 13/06/2012, SP5 to SP8 17/06/2012. The crepuscular peak is stated only in the Abstract; Results and Discussion do not state it (Figure 3 gives hourly detection percentages without naming a peak).

value: activity generally peaked around dusk and dawn, with most activities ±2 h from sunrise/sunset
method: passive acoustic telemetry (Vemco receivers) on wild-caught, surgically tagged and released fish; individual diel activity from detections
conditions: Wild common lionfish in their native range, sub-tropical fringing reef off Eilat, Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea; 13 Vemco receivers deployed May 2017 to February 2019. 11 fish tagged, 8 survived and their detections were analysed. Fish captured at night by SCUBA divers with hand nets, kept in a 700 L lab tank with fresh seawater circulation until tagged the following morning (up to 10 h from capture), returned to the tank for at least 36 h after tag implantation, then released at the original capture point (±50 m). The paper's finding is large individual-level variability in activity hours; individuals often changed their patterns over time (low repeatability); depth preference also varied among individuals. The abstract also notes that nocturnal individuals from deeper waters possibly replenishing diurnally culled shallow populations. Next Results sentence: some activity almost throughout the entire day, some individuals tending to nocturnal activity (e.g., fish #5), some toward diurnal activity (e.g., fish #1), others mainly crepuscular. Abstract: although all tracked fish were active during both sunrise and sunset, certain individuals had prolonged activity hours to variable extents. Introduction: lionfish traditionally described as crepuscular at a population level.
